edges.note: pair 1 unequal: early return, no call, counter untouched
pair 1 equal, pair 2 unequal: early return, no call
pairs 1-2 equal, pair 3 unequal: early return, no call
pairs 1-3 equal, pair 4 unequal: early return, no call
pairs 1-4 equal, pair 5 unequal: early return, no call
all five pairs equal: call once, counter decremented
all five pairs equal, counter zero: 32-bit wrap to 0xffffffff
all five pairs equal, counter high bit: decremented to 0x7fffffff

rule.summary: Let inner = [rdi] and second = [rdi+8]. If any of the five qword pairs ([inner+8],[inner+0x10]), ([inner+0x38],[inner+0x40]), ([inner+0x68],[inner+0x70]), ([inner+0x80],[inner+0x88]), ([inner+0xb0],[inner+0xb8]) is unequal, return with no call and no counter change. If all five pairs are equal, call 0x5334d60 with rdi = second+0x700, then decrement the dword at [second+0x149c] by 1 (32-bit wrap) and return. No return value is claimed: rax holds the inner pointer on early paths and the second pointer on the call path.
